transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-20
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Tom Rios (Aegis Head of ML), Priya Kapoor (Platform Eng), Ellen Park (CISO)

Summary: quick POC scoping focused on cost/unit economics, expected workload sizing, benchmark plan, and timelines. Customer looking at Dedicated vs Hosted with strong data controls (VPC + KMS). They want to validate per-token economics and latency under 200-300ms tail for user-facing flows.

Topics: success criteria, qps and concurrency, avg tokens in/out, prefix caching, batch size knobs, expected unit cost ranges, benchmark plan, procurement timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is maya from Redwood, we have diego with me from the infra team. quick confirm on attendees?
[00:09] Tom Rios: yeah hey, tom here, priya and ellen on as well. thanks for doing this.
[00:13] Priya Kapoor: hi
[00:14] Ellen Park: hello
[00:17] Diego Alvarez: cool, goal for today is to scope the poc — sizing, metrics, and a realistic cost model so we can hand you a spreadsheet you can plug into procurement.
[00:26] Tom Rios: perfect. high level — we're building an assistant inside our trading dashboard, user-facing, so latency matters. target p95 under 250ms ideally. throughput starts small, maybe 50 qps peak, but could burst. average prompt size about 120 tokens, response around 280 tokens so ~400 tokens per request.
[00:47] Maya Chen: ok that's helpful. so 50 qps x 400 tokens = ~20k tokens/sec, right? rough monthly tokens at steady-state would be in the tens of billions, we'll show a couple of scenarios.
[00:59] Tom Rios: correct, and budget is constrained — we're aiming to keep cloud inference under $100k/month initially.
[01:06] Priya Kapoor: also important: data residency and KMS, we need audit logs; prefer dedicated pool but open to hosted if there's adequate isolation.
[01:16] Maya Chen: understood, we usually recommend starting hosted to validate model/ prompts then move to a Dedicated pool to get predictable unit costs. diego, can you walk through the knobs that affect per token cost?
[01:26] Diego Alvarez: sure. main levers are batching (inference throughput), prefix or KV caching (saves tokens for repeated context), model size / quantization (smaller model = cheaper tokens), and the routing policy — whether requests go to a lower-cost variant when latency allows. also hardware selection — A10 vs A100 vs H100 equivalents change cost per token.
[01:44] Tom Rios: when you say batching — that increases latency right? how do we balance p95 latency vs cost?
[01:50] Diego Alvarez: yep, batching trades a little latency for much lower cost per token. with continuous batching and a target SLO we can cap batch windows to 10-20ms to keep p95 within your 250ms target. for user-facing, we recommend small batch sizes + prefix cache to get both cost savings and latency.
[02:05] Priya Kapoor: prefix cache — we have a lot of repeated system prompts and templates; that should help.
[02:10] Diego Alvarez: exactly. if you can identify the portion of context that's repeated, KV cache can avoid re-computation for that prefix, saving x% of compute. in our past benchmarks we saw 20-40% token compute reduction depending on prompt reuse.
[02:23] Maya Chen: on units, for modeling purposes today we'll use two price points: hosted baseline and Dedicated reserved pool. ballpark hosted inference cost per token for the model class you're likely to use (open 70B quantized) is around $0.000015 per token; Dedicated can drop unit cost by 20-40% depending on commit and hardware. these are ballparks — the spreadsheet will have exact math.
[02:47] Tom Rios: ok so with 20k tokens/sec and $0.000015/token that is roughly $777k/month? (inaudible) can you run the math? feels high.
[02:58] Diego Alvarez: quick calc yes — 20k tokens/s * 2,592,000 seconds/month = 51.84B tokens/month. * $0.000015 = $777,600. that's steady 50 qps all month; if you have 'peaky' traffic it's lower on average. we need to model real usage curves — for example 4 hours/day peak 50 qps and lower baseline the rest.
[03:19] Priya Kapoor: that exceeds our $100k goal. what levers to bring it down?
[03:23] Maya Chen: a few: optimize prompts to reduce tokens, use prefix/KV caching, switch to a cheaper model variant for lower-latency or lower-sensitivity paths, use Dedicated reserved capacity to get 20-40% cost reduction, and aggressive batching for non-user-critical flows. also consider caching final responses for repeated queries.
[03:39] Tom Rios: what's realistically achievable? if we optimize prompts and use caching, can we get under $100k?
[03:44] Diego Alvarez: hypothetically, with 50% effective token reduction across the workload (prompt compression + cache + response truncation) + a 30% Dedicated discount, you can get close. e.g., 51.84B tokens -> 25.9B effective tokens * $0.0000105 (after discount) ≈ $272k. still above 100k but much better. to hit 100k you'd need either lower sustained qps (e.g., 15 qps average) or more aggressive caching / model substitution.
[04:09] Ellen Park: from compliance side we also need e2e encryption with customer KMS and audit logs — that may push us to Dedicated or Private deploy.
[04:18] Maya Chen: totally. for Private deploy (on-prem/VPC) unit economics differ — infra cost more hands-on but you get control and can amortize if you already own GPUs. procurement often chooses Dedicated as a middle ground: predictable costs + Redwood handles infra.
[04:31] Priya Kapoor: benchmark plan?
[04:33] Diego Alvarez: propose: 48-hour benchmark with synthetic traffic that mirrors your distribution. two phases: latency-focused (small batch, low queue) to measure p95/p99, then throughput-focused (larger batch windows) to measure cost per 1k tokens and max throughput. we'll run hosted baseline then replicate on Dedicated config with identical model bits.
[04:50] Tom Rios: we'll provide a sample prompt set and trace of real traffic (anonymized) — is that enough to get a realistic number?
[04:55] Diego Alvarez: yes, traces + sample prompts plus target SLOs. Diego: also we should instrument token-level breakdown so you can see where tokens are spent (system prompts, user prompt, generation). that helps prioritization.
[05:06] Maya Chen: we'll deliver a cost-model spreadsheet with scenarios (steady vs peak, cache effectiveness, model variant). Maya: i'll send pricing deck and security pack after the call.
[05:14] Tom Rios: timeline — we want a 4 week POC. week 1: baseline tests & sample data ingestion; week 2: hosted prompt tuning and caching config; week 3: Dedicated proof and cost run; week 4: run final benchmarks and decision.
[05:27] Priya Kapoor: that works, procurement cycle is ~6 weeks after POC.
[05:30] Ellen Park: procurement will need SOC2 + data flow diagrams and contract language for KMS.
[05:35] Maya Chen: noted — we'll include those in the security pack.
[05:38] Tom Rios: any blockers on our side?
[05:40] Priya Kapoor: we'll need the exact sample format for the prompt traces.
[05:43] Diego Alvarez: i'll follow up with a template for traces and a runbook for the benchmark; we'll also include suggested Continuous Batch settings and KV cache configs to try.
[05:53] Tom Rios: quick question on model variants: can we route low-risk queries to a smaller 13B model and keep high-sensitivity queries on the 70B?
[06:01] Diego Alvarez: absolutely — smart routing by policy is one of our features. you can tag requests and route to cheaper models when acceptable, with automatic fallback.
[06:09] Priya Kapoor: does Redwood provide tooling to measure token savings from cache before we run full POC?
[06:14] Maya Chen: yes we have profiler that can run against a sample set and estimate effective cache hit rate; we'll include that in the deliverables.
[06:20] Ellen Park: procurement will also ask for a sample SLA for Dedicated — uptime and latency SLOs.
[06:25] Maya Chen: we can provide the Dedicated SLA draft. default uptime 99.9% with escalation policy; latency SLOs depend on model/hardware configs but we'll surface targets.
[06:35] Tom Rios: ok, let's recap next steps.
[06:37] Maya Chen: recap: i'll send pricing sheet, security pack, and cost-model spreadsheet by tomorrow (Maya). diego will run a 48h benchmark on a small Dedicated pool once we agree on traces (diego). tom to share sample prompts and traffic traces. ellen to confirm compliance checklist items. schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-09-07.
[06:58] Tom Rios: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:00] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

References & Links mentioned: Pricing deck (link shared in chat), Cost-model spreadsheet (will be shared), Security pack / SOC2 artifacts (link to secure drop), benchmark runbook (internal link).
